translations.literal: Biography 58: Imperial Affinity Kin — Shi Jianu, Pei Manda, Hu Du, Tudan Gong, Wugulun Puluhu, Tangkuo Dewen, Wugulun Zhanmeihe, Pucha Ahudie, Wulinda Hui, Pucha Dingshou, Tudan Sizhong, Tudan Yi, Wulinda Fu, Wugulun Yuanzhong's son Yi, Tangkuo Gong, Wulinda Lin, Tudan Gongbi, Tudan Ming, Tudan Sixi
translations.idiomatic: Biography 58: Consort Kin — Shi Jianu; Pei Manda; Hu Du; Tudan Gong; Wugulun Puluhu; Tangkuo Dewen; Wugulun Zhanmeihe; Pucha Ahudie; Wulinda Hui; Pucha Dingshou; Tudan Sizhong; Tudan Yi; Wulinda Fu; Yi, son of Wugulun Yuanzhong; Tangkuo Gong; Wulinda Lin; Tudan Gongbi; Tudan Ming; and Tudan Sixi

sentences.zh: 金昭祖娶徒單氏，后妃之族，自此始見。

translations.literal: Jin Emperor Zhaozu married a woman of the Tudan clan; the families of empresses and consorts first appear in the record from this time.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozu of Jin took a wife from the Tudan clan; it is from this marriage that consort kin first enter the histories.

sentences.zh: 世祖時，烏春為難，世祖欲求昏以結其歡心，烏春曰：「女直與胡里改豈可為昏。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Shizu, Wuchun made trouble; Shizu wished to seek a marriage alliance to win his goodwill, but Wuchun said: "How can Jurchen and Hurile become marriage kin?"
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Shizu, Wuchun stirred up conflict; Shizu tried to seal a marriage alliance to win him over, but Wuchun replied, "How can Jurchen and Hurile ever marry into one another?"

sentences.zh: 」世宗時，賜夾穀清臣族同國人。

translations.literal: " In the time of Emperor Shizong, the clan of Jiagu Qingchen was granted the status of fellow-countrymen.
translations.idiomatic: " Later, under Emperor Shizong, the clan of Jiagu Qingchen was granted the same standing as native Jurchen.

sentences.zh: 清臣，胡里改人也。

translations.literal: Qingchen was a man of Hurile.
translations.idiomatic: Qingchen himself was from Hurile.

sentences.zh: 然則四十七部之中亦有不通昏因者矣，其故則莫能詰也。

translations.literal: Thus even among the forty-seven divisions there were those who did not intermarry, but the reason cannot be fully investigated.
translations.idiomatic: So even among the forty-seven tribal divisions there were groups that did not intermarry, though the reason for this cannot now be fully traced.

sentences.zh: 有國家者，昏因有恆族，能使風氣淳固，親義不渝，而貴賤等威有別焉，蓋良法也歟。

translations.literal: For a state, fixed clans for marriage alliances can make customs pure and firm, kinship obligations unchanging, and noble and humble each with their proper dignity — is this not a good law?
translations.idiomatic: For any polity, reserving marriage alliances to fixed clans can keep customs wholesome, kinship bonds steadfast, and rank and precedence clearly distinguished — perhaps this is sound policy after all.

sentences.zh: 作《世戚傳》。

translations.literal: Therefore the "Biographies of Imperial Affinity Kin" was composed.
translations.idiomatic: Hence this "Biographies of Consort Kin."

sentences.zh: 石家奴

translations.literal: Shi Jianu
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jianu

sentences.zh: 石家奴，蒲察部人，世居案出虎水。

translations.literal: Shi Jianu was a man of the Pucha division and for generations dwelt on the Anchuhu River.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jianu belonged to the Pucha tribe and his family had long lived on the Anchuhu River.

sentences.zh: 祖斛魯短，世祖外孫。

translations.literal: His grandfather Huluoduan was a grandson by a daughter of Emperor Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Huluoduan was Emperor Shizu's grandson by a daughter.

sentences.zh: 桓赧、散達之亂，昭肅皇后父母兄弟皆在敵境，斛魯短以計迎還之。

translations.literal: In the disorders of Huang'an and Sanda, the parents and brothers of Empress Zhaosu were all in enemy territory; Huluoduan by stratagem brought them back.
translations.idiomatic: During the rebellions of Huang'an and Sanda, Empress Zhaosu's parents and brothers were all trapped behind enemy lines; Huluoduan contrived to bring them safely home.

sentences.zh: 石家奴自幼時撫養于太祖家，及長，太祖以女妻之。

translations.literal: Shi Jianu from childhood was reared in the house of Taizu; when he grew up, Taizu gave him a daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jianu was raised from childhood in Taizu's household, and when he came of age Taizu gave him a princess in marriage.

sentences.zh: 年十五，從攻甯江州，敗遼主親軍，攻臨潢府皆有功，襲謀克。

translations.literal: At age fifteen he followed the attack on Ningjiang Prefecture, defeated the Liao emperor's personal army, and had merit in the assault on Linhuang Prefecture; he inherited the office of mouke.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he took part in the assault on Ningjiang, routed the Liao emperor's personal guard, distinguished himself at Linhuang, and inherited his father's mouke command.

sentences.zh: 其後，自山西護齊國王謀良虎之喪歸上京，道由興中。

translations.literal: Later, returning from Shanxi where he had escorted the funeral of Prince Qi, Moulianghu, to the Upper Capital, he passed through Xingzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while escorting the funeral of Prince Qi Moulianghu from Shanxi back to the Upper Capital, he traveled by way of Xingzhong.

sentences.zh: 是時，方攻興中未下，石家奴置柩于驛，率其所領猛安兵助王師，遂破其城。

translations.literal: At that time the assault on Xingzhong had not yet succeeded; Shi Jianu left the coffin at the post station, led the meng'an troops under his command to aid the imperial army, and so took the city.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzhong was still under siege; Shi Jianu left the bier at the relay station, led his meng'an troops to reinforce the imperial forces, and helped capture the city.

sentences.zh: 從宗望討張覺。

translations.literal: He followed Zongwang in the campaign against Zhang Jue.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Zongwang against Zhang Jue.

sentences.zh: 再從宗翰伐宋。

translations.literal: Again he followed Zonghan in the invasion of Song.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Zonghan in the war against Song.

sentences.zh: 宗翰聞宗望軍已圍汴，遣石家奴計事，抵平定軍遇敵兵數萬，敗之，遂見宗望。

translations.literal: Zonghan, hearing that Zongwang's army had already besieged Bian, sent Shi Jianu to consult on affairs; reaching Pingding Army he met tens of thousands of enemy troops, defeated them, and then saw Zongwang.
translations.idiomatic: When Zonghan learned that Zongwang had already invested Bian, he sent Shi Jianu to coordinate plans; at Pingding Army Shi Jianu met an enemy force of tens of thousands, routed it, and then joined Zongwang.

sentences.zh: 已還報，宗翰聞其平定之戰，甚嘉之。

translations.literal: After he returned to report, Zonghan heard of the battle at Pingding and greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: On his return with the report, Zonghan heard of the victory at Pingding and praised him highly.

sentences.zh: 明年，復伐宋，石家奴隸婁室軍。

translations.literal: The next year, when Song was again invaded, Shi Jianu served under Loushi's army.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, in the renewed campaign against Song, he served under Loushi.

sentences.zh: 婁室討陝西未下，石家奴領所部兵援之。

translations.literal: Loushi's pacification of Shaanxi had not yet succeeded; Shi Jianu led the troops of his command to reinforce him.
translations.idiomatic: Loushi's operations in Shaanxi had stalled; Shi Jianu led his own troops to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 既而，以本部屯戍西京，會契丹大石出奔，以余睹為元帥，石家奴為副，襲諸部族以還。

translations.literal: Soon after, with his own command he garrisoned the Western Capital; when the Khitan Dashi fled, Yudu was made commander-in-chief and Shi Jianu deputy, and they raided the various tribes and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He was then stationed with his command at the Western Capital; when the Khitan prince Dashi fled west, Yudu was appointed commander-in-chief with Shi Jianu as his deputy, and they raided the tribal groups before returning.

sentences.zh: 未幾，有疾，退居鄉里。

translations.literal: Before long he fell ill and retired to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he fell ill and retired to his native place.

sentences.zh: 天眷間，授侍中、駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: During the Tianjuan era he was appointed Palace Attendant and Commandant of the Imperial Sons-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianjuan period he was made palace attendant and commandant of the imperial sons-in-law.

sentences.zh: 再以都統定邊部，熙宗賜御書嘉獎之。

translations.literal: Again as commander-in-chief he pacified the frontier tribes; Emperor Xizong bestowed an imperial letter commending him.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as frontier commander-in-chief, and Emperor Xizong rewarded him with an imperial letter of commendation.

sentences.zh: 封蘭陵郡王。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Lanling Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Lanling.

sentences.zh: 除東京留守，以病致仕。

translations.literal: He was appointed military governor of the Eastern Capital but retired on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed military governor of the Eastern Capital but retired because of illness.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十三，加贈鄖王。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-three and was posthumously ennobled as Prince of Yun.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-three and was posthumously ennobled as Prince of Yun.

sentences.zh: 正隆奪王爵，封魯國公。

translations.literal: Under Zhenglong his princely rank was revoked and he was enfeoffed as Duke of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenglong reign his princely title was stripped and he was posthumously made Duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 裴滿達

translations.literal: Pei Manda
translations.idiomatic: Pei Manda

sentences.zh: 忽睹，天眷三年權猛安，皇統元年為行軍猛安。

translations.literal: Hu Du, in the third year of Tianjuan served as acting meng'an; in the first year of Huangtong he became campaigning meng'an.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Du served as acting meng'an in the third year of Tianjuan and as campaigning meng'an in the first year of Huangtong.

sentences.zh: 曆橫海、崇義軍節度使，以後戚怙勢贓汙不法。

translations.literal: He successively served as military governor of the Henghai and Chongyi armies; as a consort kinsman he relied on his position, taking bribes and breaking the law.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as military governor of Henghai and Chongyi; as an imperial in-law he abused his power, taking bribes and flouting the law.

sentences.zh: 其在橫海，拜富人為父，及死，為之行服而分其資。

translations.literal: While at Henghai he acknowledged a rich man as his father; when the man died he wore mourning for him and divided his property.
translations.idiomatic: At Henghai he ceremonially adopted a wealthy man as his father; when the man died he donned mourning garb and seized a share of the estate.

sentences.zh: 在崇義，諷寺僧設齋而受其施。

translations.literal: At Chongyi he prompted temple monks to hold feasts and accepted their offerings.
translations.idiomatic: At Chongyi he induced temple monks to hold banquets and pocketed their donations.

sentences.zh: 及留守中京，益驕恣，苟可以得財無不為者。

translations.literal: When he became defender of the Central Capital he grew still more arrogant and unrestrained; whatever could yield money he did.
translations.idiomatic: As defender of the Central Capital he grew still more arrogant and would stoop to any scheme that brought him profit.

sentences.zh: 選諸猛安富人子弟為紮野，規取財物，時號「閑郎君」。

translations.literal: He selected sons of rich families from the various meng'an as zhaye attendants to scheme for goods, and at the time was called the "Idle Young Lord."
translations.idiomatic: He recruited sons of wealthy meng'an families as personal attendants to extort wealth and was nicknamed the "Idle Young Lord."

sentences.zh: 朝廷以忽睹與徒單恭等汙濫至甚，命秉德黜陟天下官吏，忽睹以贓罷。

translations.literal: The court, because Hu Du and Tudan Gong and others had been corrupt to an extreme degree, ordered Bingde to promote and demote officials throughout the realm; Hu Du was dismissed for bribery.
translations.idiomatic: Because Hu Du, Tudan Gong, and others had grown so corrupt, the court ordered Bingde to review officials empire-wide; Hu Du was removed for bribery.

sentences.zh: 海陵以忽睹所至縱家奴擾民，乃定禁外官任所閒雜人條約。

translations.literal: Hailing, because wherever Hu Du went he let household slaves harass the people, thereupon fixed regulations forbidding idle hangers-on in the jurisdictions of outside officials.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing, noting that Hu Du's household slaves had harassed the populace wherever he served, promulgated rules restricting retainers and idlers in the jurisdictions of provincial officials.

sentences.zh: 天德三年，復起為鄭州防禦使，改安國軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiande he was again raised up as defender-in-chief of Zhengzhou and then transferred to military governor of the Anguo army.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tiande he was reappointed defender-in-chief of Zhengzhou and later made military governor of Anguo.

sentences.zh: 卒，年三十九。

translations.literal: He died at age thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 徒單恭

translations.literal: Tudan Gong
translations.idiomatic: Tudan Gong

sentences.zh: 徒單恭，本名斜也。

translations.literal: Tudan Gong, original name Xieye.
translations.idiomatic: Tudan Gong, whose original name was Xieye.

sentences.zh: 天眷二年，為奉國上將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianjuan he was made General-in-Chief Who Supports the State.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianjuan he was appointed general-in-chief who supports the state.

sentences.zh: 以告吳十反事，超授龍虎衛上將軍。

translations.literal: For reporting Wu Shi's rebellion he was specially promoted to General-in-Chief of the Dragon-Tiger Guard.
translations.idiomatic: For exposing Wu Shi's plot to rebel he was specially promoted to general-in-chief of the Dragon-Tiger Guard.

sentences.zh: 為戶部侍郎，出為濟南尹，遷會甯牧，封譚國公。

translations.literal: He served as vice minister of revenue, went out as prefect of Jinan, was transferred to be herdsman of Huining, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Tan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice minister of revenue, was sent out as prefect of Jinan, then transferred to herdsman of Huining and enfeoffed as Duke of Tan.

sentences.zh: 復出為太原尹。

translations.literal: He again went out as prefect of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was again posted as prefect of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 斜也貪鄙，使工繪一佛像，自稱嘗見佛，其像如此，當以金鑄之。

translations.literal: Xieye was greedy and base; he had artisans paint a Buddha image, claiming he had once seen the Buddha and that the image was like this and should be cast in gold.
translations.idiomatic: Xieye was grasping and mean; he had craftsmen paint a Buddha image, claiming he had seen the Buddha and that it should be cast in gold.

sentences.zh: 遂賦屬縣金，而未嘗鑄佛，盡入其家，百姓號為「金總管」。

translations.literal: He then levied gold on the subordinate counties but never cast the Buddha; it all went into his household, and the people called him the "Gold Commander."
translations.idiomatic: He levied gold from the counties under him but never cast the image; the gold went entirely into his own coffers, and the people dubbed him the "Gold Commander."

sentences.zh: 秉德廉訪官吏，斜也以贓免。

translations.literal: Bingde conducted an integrity inspection of officials; Xieye was dismissed for bribery.
translations.idiomatic: When Bingde inspected officials for corruption, Xieye was dismissed for bribery.

sentences.zh: 海陵篡立，海陵後徒單氏，斜也女，由是復用為會甯牧，封王。

translations.literal: When Hailing usurped the throne, Hailing's empress was of the Tudan clan — Xieye's daughter — and for this reason he was again employed as herdsman of Huining and enfeoffed as prince.
translations.idiomatic: After Hailing seized the throne, his empress was Xieye's daughter of the Tudan clan; Xieye was therefore restored as herdsman of Huining and enfeoffed as a prince.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜平章政事，海陵獵于胡剌渾水，斜也編列圍場，凡平日不相能者輒杖之。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed chief councilor; when Hailing hunted on the Hulahun River, Xieye arranged the hunting enclosure and beat with the staff anyone with whom he was not on good terms in ordinary times.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made chief councilor; when Hailing hunted on the Hulahun River, Xieye laid out the beat and had anyone he disliked beaten with the staff.

sentences.zh: 海陵謂宰相曰：「斜也為相，朕非私之。

translations.literal: Hailing said to the chief ministers: "Xieye serves as councilor, and I am not favoring him privately.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing told the chief ministers, "I appointed Xieye as councilor without favoritism.

sentences.zh: 今聞軍國大事凡斜也所言，卿等一無取，豈千慮無一得乎？

translations.literal: Now I hear that in military and state affairs, whatever Xieye says, you take none of it — can it be that in a thousand deliberations not one is right?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet I hear that on every matter of state you reject whatever he proposes — can he truly never be right?"

sentences.zh: 」他宰相無以對，溫都思忠舉數事對曰：「某事本當如此，斜也輒以為如彼，皆妄生異議，不達事宜。

translations.literal: " The other chief ministers had nothing to reply; Wendusi Zhong cited several matters and answered: "Such-and-such a matter should originally have been thus, but Xieye insistently held it should be so-and-so — all were groundless objections, not understanding what the situation required.
translations.idiomatic: " The other ministers were silent; Wendusi Zhong answered with several examples: "On this matter the right course was clear, yet Xieye insisted on the opposite — empty objections every time, with no grasp of policy.

sentences.zh: 臣逮事康宗，累朝宰相未嘗有如斜也專恣者。

translations.literal: Your servant has served since Emperor Kangzong; through successive reigns there has never been a chief minister as willful as Xieye."
translations.idiomatic: I have served since Emperor Kangzong's day, and through successive reigns I have never seen a chief minister as overbearing as Xieye."

sentences.zh: 」海陵默然。

translations.literal: " Hailing was silent.
translations.idiomatic: " Hailing said nothing.

sentences.zh: 斜也於都堂脊杖令史馮仲尹，御史臺劾之，海陵杖之二十。

translations.literal: Xieye at the chief council hall beat the clerk Feng Zhongyin with a staff on the back; the censorate impeached him, and Hailing had him beaten twenty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Xieye beat the chief council clerk Feng Zhongyin with a staff in the hall; the censorate impeached him, and Hailing had Xieye beaten twenty strokes.

sentences.zh: 斜也猛安部人撒合出者，言斜也強率取部人財物。

translations.literal: Sahechu, a man of Xieye's meng'an division, said that Xieye had forcibly taken the property of men of the division.
translations.idiomatic: Sahechu, a man of Xieye's meng'an division, accused him of forcibly seizing the property of his tribesmen.

sentences.zh: 海陵命侍御史保魯鞫之。

translations.literal: Hailing ordered the attendant censor Baolu to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing ordered the attendant censor Baolu to investigate.

sentences.zh: 保魯鞫不以實，海陵杖保魯，而以撒合出為符寶祗候，改隸合紮猛安。

translations.literal: Baolu investigated without finding the facts; Hailing beat Baolu and made Sahechu an attendant of the imperial seals and changed his affiliation to the Hezha meng'an.
translations.idiomatic: Baolu failed to establish the facts; Hailing had Baolu beaten and appointed Sahechu attendant of the imperial seals, transferring him to the Hezha meng'an.

sentences.zh: 斜也兄定哥尚太祖長女兀魯，定哥死無子，以季弟之子查剌為後。

translations.literal: Xieye's elder brother Dingge had married Taizu's eldest daughter Wulu; Dingge died without sons, and the youngest brother's son Zhacha was made heir.
translations.idiomatic: Xieye's elder brother Dingge had married Taizu's eldest daughter Wulu; when Dingge died childless, the youngest brother's son Zhacha was adopted as heir.

sentences.zh: 斜也謀取其兄家財，強納兀魯為室而不相能，兀魯嘗怨詈斜也。

translations.literal: Xieye plotted to seize his brother's family wealth, forcibly took Wulu as wife though they could not get along, and Wulu often cursed Xieye in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Xieye schemed to seize his brother's estate, forced Wulu to marry him though they loathed each other, and Wulu often cursed him in anger.

sentences.zh: 斜也妾忽撻與兀魯不葉，乃譖兀魯於海陵後徒單氏曰：「兀魯怨上殺其兄宗敏，有怨望語。

translations.literal: Xieye's concubine Hut'a was at odds with Wulu; she slandered Wulu to Hailing's empress Tudan, saying: "Wulu resents that the emperor killed her brother Zongmin and has words of resentment."
translations.idiomatic: Xieye's concubine Hut'a hated Wulu and slandered her to Empress Tudan, saying, "Wulu blames the emperor for killing her brother Zongmin and has spoken resentfully of the throne."

sentences.zh: 」會韓王亨改廣甯尹，諸公主宗婦往賀其母，兀魯以言慰亨母，忽撻亦以怨望指斥誣兀魯。

translations.literal: " It happened that Prince Han, Xiang, was transferred to be prefect of Guangning; the various princesses and imperial daughters-in-law went to congratulate his mother; Wulu spoke words of consolation to Xiang's mother, and Hut'a also accused Wulu with charges of resentment.
translations.idiomatic: " When Prince Han Xiang was reassigned as prefect of Guangning, the princesses and imperial daughters-in-law went to congratulate his mother; Wulu offered words of comfort to the prince's mother, and Hut'a again accused her of disloyal speech.

sentences.zh: 海陵使蕭裕鞫之，忽撻得幸于徒單後，左驗皆不敢言，遂殺兀魯，斜也因而盡奪查剌家財。

translations.literal: Hailing had Xiao Yu investigate; Hut'a enjoyed favor with Empress Tudan, and corroborating witnesses all dared not speak; Wulu was then killed, and Xieye thereby seized all of Zhacha's family property.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing had Xiao Yu investigate; because Hut'a was favored by the empress, witnesses dared not testify; Wulu was executed, and Xieye seized all of Zhacha's inheritance.

sentences.zh: 大定間皆追正之。

translations.literal: In the Dading era all were posthumously rectified.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Shizong's Dading reign all these wrongs were posthumously redressed.

sentences.zh: 海陵以兀魯有怨望語，斜也不奏，遂杖斜也，免所居官。

translations.literal: Hailing, because Wulu had words of resentment, and Xieye had not reported them, thereupon beat Xieye and removed him from his office.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wulu had spoken resentfully and Xieye had failed to report it, Hailing had Xieye beaten and dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 俄，復為司徒，進拜太保，領三省事，兼勸農使。

translations.literal: Soon he was again made Minister of Education, advanced to Grand Mentor, headed the Three Departments, and concurrently served as agricultural commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was restored as minister of education, promoted to grand mentor, placed over the Three Departments, and made agricultural commissioner as well.

sentences.zh: 再進太師，封梁晉國王。

translations.literal: He was again advanced to Grand Preceptor and enfeoffed as Prince of Liang and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to grand preceptor and enfeoffed as Prince of Liang and Jin.

sentences.zh: 其妻先斜也卒，海陵嘗至其葬所致祭，起復其子率府率吾裏補為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: His wife died before Xieye; Hailing once came to the burial place to offer sacrifice, and on mourning leave his son Wulibu, chamberlain of the leading palace, was recalled to serve as remonstrating grand master.
translations.idiomatic: His wife predeceased him; Hailing once attended her burial to offer sacrifice, and recalled his son Wulibu from mourning to serve as remonstrating grand master.

sentences.zh: 大定間，海陵降為庶人，徒單氏為庶人妻，斜也降特進鞏國公。

translations.literal: In the Dading era Hailing was reduced to commoner status, the Tudan clan became a commoner's wife, and Xieye was reduced to specially advanced Duke of Gong.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dading period Hailing was posthumously reduced to commoner rank, his empress of the Tudan clan to a commoner's wife, and Xieye to specially advanced Duke of Gong.

sentences.zh: 烏古論蒲魯虎

translations.literal: Wugulun Puluhu
translations.idiomatic: Wugulun Puluhu

sentences.zh: 烏古論蒲魯虎，父當海，國初有功。

translations.literal: Wugulun Puluhu — his father Danghai had merit at the founding of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Wugulun Puluhu was the son of Danghai, who had earned distinction in the founding of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 蒲魯虎通契丹大小字，娶宋王宗望女昭甯公主什古。

translations.literal: Puluhu mastered the large and small Khitan scripts and married Princess Zhaoning Shigu, daughter of Prince Song Zongwang.
translations.idiomatic: Puluhu mastered both Khitan scripts and married Princess Zhaoning Shigu, daughter of Prince Song Zongwang.

sentences.zh: 熙宗初，為護衛，改牌印，常侍左右。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xizong's reign he was an imperial guard, then changed to keeper of seals and constantly attended at the ruler's side.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xizong's reign he served in the imperial guard, then as keeper of the seals, always attending the emperor.

sentences.zh: 轉通進。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be a senior attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to senior attendant.

sentences.zh: 襲父謀克，再遷臨海軍節度使，改衛州防禦使。

translations.literal: He inherited his father's mouke, was twice transferred to military governor of the Linhai army, and then made defender-in-chief of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father's mouke command, served twice as military governor of Linhai, and was then appointed defender-in-chief of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 海陵賜食內殿，謂之曰：「衛州風土甚佳，勿以防禦為降也。

translations.literal: Hailing granted him food in the inner hall and said to him: "The climate and land of Weizhou are very fine — do not regard the post of defender as a demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing entertained him in the inner palace and said, "Weizhou is a fine posting — do not treat the defender's rank as a demotion.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「頗聞衛州官署不利守者。

translations.literal: " He replied: "I have often heard that the official quarters at Weizhou are unlucky for those who hold them."
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "I have heard that the yamen at Weizhou is unlucky for its occupants."

sentences.zh: 」即日改汾陽軍節度使，賜衣服、佩玉、帶劍。

translations.literal: " That same day he was changed to military governor of the Fenyang army and was given robes, girdle jade, and a sword.
translations.idiomatic: " That same day he was made military governor of Fenyang and granted robes, girdle jade, and a sword.

sentences.zh: 入為太子詹事，卒，年四十一。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as tutor of the heir apparent and died at age forty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as tutor of the heir apparent and died at forty-one.

sentences.zh: 海陵親臨哭之，后妃皆弔祭，賻贈甚厚。

translations.literal: Hailing personally came to weep for him; empresses and consorts all sent condolences; funeral gifts were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing came in person to mourn him; the empresses and consorts all sent condolences; the funeral gifts were lavish.

sentences.zh: 有司給喪事，贈特進駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: The relevant offices provided the funeral; he was posthumously given the title of specially advanced commandant of the imperial sons-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities arranged the funeral and posthumously granted him the title of specially advanced commandant of the imperial sons-in-law.

sentences.zh: 正隆例贈光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Under Zhenglong, by precedent he was posthumously given Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhenglong he was posthumously granted the title of grand master of splendid happiness by precedent.

sentences.zh: 唐括德溫

translations.literal: Tangkuo Dewen
translations.idiomatic: Tangkuo Dewen

sentences.zh: 唐括德溫，本名阿里，上京率河人也。

translations.literal: Tangkuo Dewen, original name Ali, was a man of Shuaihe in the Upper Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Tangkuo Dewen, whose original name was Ali, was from Shuaihe in the Upper Capital.

sentences.zh: 曾祖石古，從太祖平臘醅麻產，領謀克。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Shigu followed Taizu in pacifying Lapai Machan and held the office of mouke.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Shigu followed Taizu in pacifying Lapai Machan and held a mouke command.

sentences.zh: 祖脫孛魯，領其父謀克，從太祖伐遼，攻甯江、泰州戰有功。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tuoboluo inherited his father's mouke, followed Taizu in the campaign against Liao, and had merit in the battles at Ningjiang and Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tuoboluo inherited the family mouke, followed Taizu against Liao, and distinguished himself at Ningjiang and Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 父撻懶，尚康宗女，從宋王宗望以軍二萬收平州，至城東十里許遇敵兵甚眾，戰敗之，太祖賞賚甚厚，授行軍猛安。

translations.literal: His father Talan married a daughter of Emperor Kangzong; following Prince Song Zongwang with twenty thousand troops he recovered Pingzhou; about ten li east of the city he met a very large enemy force, defeated them in battle, and Taizu rewarded him very generously and appointed him campaigning meng'an.
translations.idiomatic: His father Talan married a daughter of Emperor Kangzong; with twenty thousand men under Prince Song Zongwang he recovered Pingzhou, and some ten li east of the city routed a large enemy force; Taizu rewarded him handsomely and appointed him campaigning meng'an.

sentences.zh: 皇統初，遷龍虎衛上將軍，歷興平、臨海等軍節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangtong he was transferred to General-in-Chief of the Dragon-Tiger Guard and successively served as military governor of the Xingping, Linhai, and other armies.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Huangtong reign he was made general-in-chief of the Dragon-Tiger Guard and served in turn as military governor of Xingping, Linhai, and other circuits.

sentences.zh: 十八年，追錄其父撻懶並德溫前後功，授其長子駙馬都尉鼎世襲西北路沒裏山猛安，徙隸泰州。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the earlier and later merits of his father Talan and of Dewen were recorded posthumously; his eldest son, Commandant of the Imperial Sons-in-Law Ding, inherited the meng'an of Meilishan on the Northwestern Route and was transferred to be subordinate to Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year the court posthumously recorded the services of his father Talan and of Dewen himself; his eldest son, Commandant Ding, inherited the Meilishan meng'an on the Northwestern Route and was reassigned under Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 烏古論粘沒曷

translations.literal: Wugulun Zhanmeihe
translations.idiomatic: Wugulun Zhanmeihe

sentences.zh: 蒲察阿虎迭

translations.literal: Pucha Ahudie
translations.idiomatic: Pucha Ahudie

sentences.zh: 烏林答暉

translations.literal: Wulinda Hui
translations.idiomatic: Wulinda Hui

sentences.zh: 蒲察鼎壽

translations.literal: Pucha Dingshou
translations.idiomatic: Pucha Dingshou

sentences.zh: 蒲察鼎壽，本名和尚，上京曷速河人，欽懷皇后父也。

translations.literal: Pucha Dingshou, original name Heshang, was a man of Hesuhu in the Upper Capital and was the father of Empress Qinhuai.
translations.idiomatic: Pucha Dingshou, whose original name was Heshang, was from Hesuhu in the Upper Capital and was the father of Empress Qinhuai.

sentences.zh: 賦性沉厚有明鑒，通契丹、漢字，長於吏事。

translations.literal: By nature he was deep and steady with clear judgment, mastered Khitan and Chinese characters, and excelled in administrative affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was by nature steady and discerning, fluent in Khitan and Chinese script, and highly capable in administration.

sentences.zh: 尚熙宗女鄭國公主。

translations.literal: He married Princess Zheng of State, daughter of Emperor Xizong.
translations.idiomatic: He married Princess Zheng, a daughter of Emperor Xizong.

sentences.zh: 貞元三年，以海陵女弟慶宜公主子加定遠大將軍，為尚衣局使，累官器物局使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenyuan, as son of Princess Qingyi, Hailing's younger sister, he was given the additional title of General Who Establishes the Distance and made director of the Bureau of Imperial Robes, rising through offices to director of the Bureau of Implements.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenyuan, as a son of Princess Qingyi, Hailing's younger sister, he was promoted to general who establishes the distance and appointed director of the Bureau of Imperial Robes, eventually rising to director of the Bureau of Implements.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，加駙馬都尉，職如故。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dading he was additionally made commandant of the imperial sons-in-law, his duties remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dading he was also made commandant of the imperial sons-in-law while retaining his existing posts.

sentences.zh: 曆符寶郎、蠡州刺史、浚州防禦使，有惠政，兩州百姓刻石紀之。

translations.literal: He successively served as attendant of the imperial seals, prefect of Li Prefecture, and defender-in-chief of Xun Prefecture; his benevolent administration led the people of both prefectures to carve stone inscriptions commemorating him.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as attendant of the imperial seals, prefect of Li, and defender-in-chief of Xun; his benevolent rule was commemorated in stone by the people of both prefectures.

sentences.zh: 遷泰甯軍節度使，歷東平府、橫海軍，入為右宣徽使，改左宣徽，授中都路昏得渾山猛安曷速木單世襲謀克。

translations.literal: He was transferred to military governor of the Taining army, served at Dongping Prefecture and the Henghai army, entered the capital as right commissioner of the palace secretariat, was changed to left commissioner, and was granted the hereditary mouke of the Hesumu dan of the Hundeshan meng'an on the Central Capital Route.
translations.idiomatic: He became military governor of Taining, served at Dongping and Henghai, entered the capital as right then left commissioner of the palace secretariat, and received the hereditary mouke of the Hesumu dan at Hundeshan on the Central Capital Route.

sentences.zh: 改河間尹。

translations.literal: He was changed to prefect of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 號令必行，豪右屏跡。

translations.literal: His orders were invariably enforced and powerful families withdrew from sight.
translations.idiomatic: His orders were enforced without fail, and local magnates vanished from public view.

sentences.zh: 有宗室居河間，侵削居民，鼎壽奏徙其族于平州，郡內大治。

translations.literal: A member of the imperial clan living in Hejian encroached on the residents; Dingshou memorialized to move his clan to Ping Prefecture, and within the commandery there was great order.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial clansman in Hejian had been encroaching on the populace; Dingshou petitioned to relocate the clan to Pingzhou, and the prefecture was brought thoroughly to order.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 上聞之深加悼惜。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he deeply mourned and regretted the loss.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, on hearing the news, mourned him deeply.

sentences.zh: 喪至香山，皇太子往奠，百官致祭，賻銀彩絹。

translations.literal: When the coffin reached Xiangshan, the crown prince went to offer sacrifice; the hundred officials sent condolences; silver and colored silks were given as funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When the funeral procession reached Xiangshan, the crown prince came to offer sacrifice, officials sent condolences, and lavish gifts of silver and silk were granted.

sentences.zh: 明昌三年，以皇后父贈太尉、越國公。

translations.literal: In the third year of Mingchang, as the empress's father he was posthumously given Grand Marshal and Duke of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Mingchang he was posthumously ennobled as grand marshal and Duke of Yue in recognition of his status as the empress's father.

sentences.zh: 鼎壽既世連姻戚，女為皇后，長子辭不失凡三尚定國、景國、道國公主。

translations.literal: Dingshou's family for generations had been linked by marriage kinship; his daughter became empress, and his eldest son Cibushi in all three marriages wed princesses of Ding, Jing, and Dao.
translations.idiomatic: The Dingshou family had long been tied to the throne by marriage; his daughter became empress, and his eldest son Cibushi married in succession the princesses of Ding, Jing, and Dao.

sentences.zh: 其寵遇如此，未嘗以富貴驕人，當時以為外戚之冠云。

translations.literal: His favor was such, yet he never used wealth and rank to lord it over others; at the time he was regarded as the foremost of the consort kin.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the favor shown his house, yet he never lorded his wealth and rank over others; contemporaries hailed him as the model among imperial in-laws.

sentences.zh: 徒單思忠

translations.literal: Tudan Sizhong
translations.idiomatic: Tudan Sizhong

sentences.zh: 徒單思忠，字良弼，本名甯慶。

translations.literal: Tudan Sizhong, style name Liangbi, original name Ningqing.
translations.idiomatic: Tudan Sizhong, courtesy name Liangbi, whose original name was Ningqing.

sentences.zh: 曾祖賽補，尚景祖女。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Saibu married a daughter of Emperor Jingzu.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Saibu married a daughter of Emperor Jingzu.

sentences.zh: 從太祖伐遼，戰歿於臨潢之渾河。

translations.literal: Following Taizu in the campaign against Liao, he died in battle on the Hun River at Linhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Taizu against Liao and fell in battle on the Hun River at Linhuang.

sentences.zh: 父賽一，尚熙宗妹。

translations.literal: His father Saiyi married a younger sister of Emperor Xizong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Saiyi married a younger sister of Emperor Xizong.

sentences.zh: 正隆末，為颭碗群牧使，契丹賊窩斡擾北邊，賽一與戰死之。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenglong he was commissioner of the Zhanwan horse herds; the Khitan bandit Wowo disturbed the northern frontier, and Saiyi died fighting him.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Zhenglong reign he was commissioner of the Zhanwan horse herds; when the Khitan rebel Wowo raided the northern frontier, Saiyi died in battle against him.

sentences.zh: 大定初，贈金吾衛上將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dading he was posthumously given General-in-Chief of the Golden Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dading reign he was posthumously made general-in-chief of the Golden Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 十九年，上追念思忠輔立功，贈驃騎衛上將軍，乃授其子鐸武功將軍、世襲中都路烏獨渾謀克。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year the emperor, recalling Sizhong's merits in assisting the heir, posthumously gave him General-in-Chief of the Flying Cavalry Guard and thereupon appointed his son Duo military merit general and hereditary mouke of Wuduhun on the Central Capital Route.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year the emperor, remembering Sizhong's service to the heir apparent, posthumously made him general-in-chief of the Flying Cavalry Guard and appointed his son Duo military merit general with the hereditary Wuduhun mouke on the Central Capital Route.

sentences.zh: 徒單繹

translations.literal: Tudan Yi
translations.idiomatic: Tudan Yi

sentences.zh: 徒單繹，本名術輩，其先上京按出虎達阿人。

translations.literal: Tudan Yi, original name Shuben, his ancestors were men of Anchuhu Da'a in the Upper Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Tudan Yi, whose original name was Shuben, came from Anchuhu Da'a in the Upper Capital.

sentences.zh: 祖撒合懣，國初有功，授隆安府路合紮謀克、奪古阿鄰猛安。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sahemen had merit at the founding of the state and was granted hezha mouke of the Long'an Prefecture Route and meng'an of Duogu'alian.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sahemen earned distinction at the founding of the dynasty and was granted hezha mouke on the Long'an route and the Duogu'alian meng'an.

sentences.zh: 繹美姿儀，通諸國語。

translations.literal: Yi had handsome bearing and mastered the languages of the various states.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was handsome in bearing and fluent in several languages.

sentences.zh: 尚熙宗第七女沈國公主。

translations.literal: He married Princess Shen of State, the seventh daughter of Emperor Xizong.
translations.idiomatic: He married Princess Shen, the seventh daughter of Emperor Xizong.

sentences.zh: 充符寶祗候，遷御院通進，授符寶郎。

translations.literal: He served as attendant of the imperial seals, was transferred to senior attendant of the imperial household, and was appointed attendant of the seals.
translations.idiomatic: He served as attendant of the imperial seals, was promoted to senior attendant of the imperial household, and appointed attendant of the seals.

sentences.zh: 曆宣德、泰安、淄州刺史，有廉名。

translations.literal: He successively served as prefect of Xuande, Tai'an, and Zi and had a reputation for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as prefect of Xuande, Tai'an, and Zi and earned a reputation for integrity.

sentences.zh: 改同知廣寧府事，以母鄂國公主憂，不赴。

translations.literal: He was changed to associate administrator of Guangning Prefecture but, on account of mourning for his mother Princess E of State, did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed associate administrator of Guangning but did not take up the post while mourning his mother, Princess E.

sentences.zh: 世宗特許以憂制中襲父封。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong specially permitted him to inherit his father's enfeoffment while still in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong specially allowed him to inherit his father's title while still in mourning.

sentences.zh: 服闕，授同知濟南府事。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed associate administrator of Jinan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended he was appointed associate administrator of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，遷棣州防禦使，以政跡聞，升臨海軍節度使，卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was transferred to defender-in-chief of Di Prefecture; his administrative record became known and he was promoted to military governor of the Linhai army, then died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he became defender-in-chief of Di; his record in office won notice, he was promoted to military governor of Linhai, and died.

sentences.zh: 繹家世貴寵，自會祖照至繹尚公主者凡四世云。

translations.literal: Yi's family for generations enjoyed noble favor; from his great-grandfather Zhao down to Yi, those who married princesses numbered four generations in all.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's family had been favored for generations: from his great-grandfather Zhao down to Yi himself, four generations in succession had married imperial princesses.

sentences.zh: 烏林答復

translations.literal: Wulinda Fu
translations.idiomatic: Wulinda Fu

sentences.zh: 烏林答復，本名阿裏剌，東平人也。

translations.literal: Wulinda Fu, original name Alila, was a man of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Wulinda Fu, whose original name was Alila, was from Dongping.

sentences.zh: 奉御出身，大定七年尚世宗第七女宛國公主，授駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: He entered service as an imperial attendant; in the seventh year of Dading he married Princess Wan of State, the seventh daughter of Emperor Shizong, and was appointed commandant of the imperial sons-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: He began as an imperial attendant; in the seventh year of Dading he married Princess Wan, the seventh daughter of Emperor Shizong, and was made commandant of the imperial sons-in-law.

sentences.zh: 改引進使、兼符寶郎，出為蠡州刺史，三遷歸德軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was changed to commissioner of introductions and concurrently attendant of the seals, went out as prefect of Li Prefecture, and after three promotions became military governor of the Guide army.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commissioner of introductions and concurrent attendant of the seals, served as prefect of Li, and after three promotions became military governor of Guide.

sentences.zh: 明昌三年，轉知興中府事，久之，為曷懶路兵馬都總管。

translations.literal: In the third year of Mingchang he was transferred to administrator of Xingzhong Prefecture; after a long time he became overall commander of troops on the Yilan Route.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Mingchang he was made administrator of Xingzhong; later he became overall commander of troops on the Yilan Route.

sentences.zh: 承安四年，拜絳陽軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Cheng'an he was appointed military governor of the Jiangyang army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Cheng'an he was appointed military governor of Jiangyang.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 烏古論元忠

translations.literal: Wugulun Yuanzhong
translations.idiomatic: Wugulun Yuanzhong

sentences.zh: 會大興府守臣闕，遂以元忠知府事。

translations.literal: It happened that the post of defender of Daxing Prefecture was vacant, and Yuanzhong was therefore put in charge of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the post of prefect of Daxing fell vacant, Yuanzhong was appointed to administer the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 有僧犯法，吏甫得置獄，皇姑梁國大長公主屬使釋之，元忠不聽，主奏其事，世宗召謂曰：「卿不徇情，甚可嘉也，治京如此，朕復何憂。

translations.literal: A monk violated the law; the clerks had just managed to put him in prison when the emperor's paternal aunt, the Grand Princess of Liang, instructed that he be released; Yuanzhong would not listen; the princess reported the matter; Shizong summoned him and said: "You did not yield to personal feeling — this is very praiseworthy; if the capital is governed thus, what have I to worry about?"
translations.idiomatic: When a monk broke the law and officials had just imprisoned him, the Grand Princess of Liang ordered his release; Yuanzhong refused. After she reported the matter, Shizong summoned him and said, "You did not bend to favoritism — that is admirable. If the capital is governed this way, what have I to fear?"

sentences.zh: 」秩滿，授吏部尚書。

translations.literal: " When his term ended he was appointed minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: " When his term ended he was appointed minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 以其子誼尚顯宗長女薛國公主。

translations.literal: Because his son Yi married Princess Xue of State, the eldest daughter of Emperor Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi had married Princess Xue, the eldest daughter of Emperor Xianzong.

sentences.zh: 十八年，擢御史大夫，授撒巴山世襲謀克。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was promoted to censor-in-chief and granted the hereditary mouke of Sabashan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was promoted to censor-in-chief and granted the hereditary Sabashan mouke.

sentences.zh: 世宗問左丞相紇石烈良弼孰可相者，良弼以元忠對，乃拜平章政事，封任國公，進尚書右丞相。

translations.literal: Shizong asked the left chief minister Hesheli Liangbi who could serve as chief councilor; Liangbi answered with Yuanzhong; he was then appointed chief councilor, enfeoffed as Duke of Ren, and advanced to right chief minister of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong asked the left chief minister Hesheli Liangbi who could serve as chief councilor, Liangbi named Yuanzhong; Yuanzhong was appointed chief councilor, enfeoffed as Duke of Ren, and promoted to right chief minister.

sentences.zh: 策論進士之科設，元忠贊成之。

translations.literal: When the examination category for policy-discourse presented scholars was established, Yuanzhong supported it.
translations.idiomatic: When the policy-discourse doctorate examination was instituted, Yuanzhong supported the reform.

sentences.zh: 世宗將幸會寧，元忠進諫不聽，出知真定府，尋復詔為右丞相。

translations.literal: When Shizong was about to visit Huining, Yuanzhong remonstrated but was not heeded; he was sent out to administer Zhending Prefecture, and soon was again ordered back as right chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong planned to visit Huining, Yuanzhong remonstrated in vain; he was sent to administer Zhending but was soon recalled as right chief minister.

sentences.zh: 世宗欲甓上京城，元忠曰：「此邦遭正隆軍興，百姓凋弊，陛下休養二十餘年，尚未完復。

translations.literal: Shizong wished to brick the walls of the Upper Capital; Yuanzhong said: "This region suffered from Zhenglong's military campaigns; the people are depleted; Your Majesty has rested and nurtured them for more than twenty years, yet recovery is still incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong wished to brick the walls of the Upper Capital, Yuanzhong said, "This region was ravaged by the wars of the Zhenglong reign; the people are still exhausted. Your Majesty has given them more than twenty years to recover, and they are not yet restored.

sentences.zh: 況土性疏惡，甓之恐難經久，風雨摧壞，歲歲繕完，民將益因矣。

translations.literal: Moreover the soil is loose and poor; if bricked it may not last long — wind and rain will destroy it, and year by year repairs will be needed; the people will be burdened still more."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the soil is poor and unstable; brickwork may not endure, and wind and rain will ruin it, forcing yearly repairs that will only burden the people further."

sentences.zh: 」駕東幸久之未還，元忠奏曰：「鸞輿駐此已閱歲，倉儲日少，市買漸貴，禁衛暨諸局署多逃者，有司捕置諸法恐傷陛下仁愛。

translations.literal: " The imperial carriage on the eastern tour long did not return; Yuanzhong memorialized: "The imperial carriage has stayed here for more than a year; granary stores daily diminish and market purchases grow costly; many of the palace guard and the various bureaus have fled; if the authorities arrest and punish by all the laws, I fear it will harm Your Majesty's benevolence."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor's eastern tour lingered for more than a year without return; Yuanzhong memorialized, "Your Majesty has been away for over a year; stores are dwindling and prices rising; many guards and bureau staff have deserted; if officials arrest them by the full rigor of the law, I fear it will wound Your Majesty's reputation for mercy."

sentences.zh: 」世宗嘉納之。

translations.literal: " Shizong praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: " Shizong praised the advice and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 尋出為北京留守，責諭之曰：「汝強悍自用，顓權而結近密。

translations.literal: Soon he went out as defender of the Northern Capital; Shizong reproved him, saying: "You are fierce and willful, monopolize power and cultivate intimates.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was sent out as defender of the Northern Capital; Shizong rebuked him, saying, "You are overbearing and willful, monopolize power, and cultivate a private circle.

sentences.zh: 汝心叵測，其速之官。

translations.literal: Your heart cannot be fathomed — go quickly to your post."
translations.idiomatic: Your intentions are impossible to read — go to your post at once."

sentences.zh: 」後左丞張汝弼奏事，世宗惡其阿順，謂左右曰：「卿等每事依違苟避，不肯盡言，高爵厚祿何以勝任。

translations.literal: " Later the left vice minister Zhang Rubi presented a memorial; Shizong disliked his flattery and said to those at his side: "You on every matter hedge and evade, unwilling to speak fully — with high rank and thick salary how can you be equal to the task?
translations.idiomatic: " Later the left vice minister Zhang Rubi presented a memorial; Shizong disliked his flattery and told his attendants, "You hedge on every issue and will not speak plainly — how can men of high rank and rich salary be fit for office?

sentences.zh: 如烏古論元忠為相，剛直敢言，義不顧身，誠可尚也。

translations.literal: Such a one as Wugulun Yuanzhong as chief councilor — upright and bold in speech, righteous without regard for his person — is truly to be honored."
translations.idiomatic: A man like Wugulun Yuanzhong as chief councilor — upright, outspoken, and ready to risk himself for principle — is truly admirable."

sentences.zh: 」於是，改知真定府事，移知河間。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he was changed to administrator of Zhending Prefecture and transferred to administer Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: " He was then reassigned to administer Zhending and later Hejian.

sentences.zh: 明昌二年，知廣寧府。

translations.literal: In the second year of Mingchang he administered Guangning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Mingchang he administered Guangning.

sentences.zh: 以河間修築球場擾民，會赦下，除順義軍節度使。

translations.literal: Because at Hejian the construction of a ball court disturbed the people, when an amnesty was issued he was made military governor of the Shunyi army.
translations.idiomatic: Because building a ball court at Hejian had harassed the populace, he was pardoned when an amnesty was proclaimed and appointed military governor of Shunyi.

sentences.zh: 乞致仕不許，特加開府儀同三司、北京留守。

translations.literal: He requested retirement but was not permitted; he was specially given Grand Master with the Golden Seal and Purple Trappings and made defender of the Northern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: His request to retire was denied; he was specially granted grand master with golden seal and purple trappings and reappointed defender of the Northern Capital.

sentences.zh: 徙知濟南府，過闕，令預宴，班平章政事之上。

translations.literal: He was transferred to administer Jinan Prefecture; passing the palace, he was ordered to attend a banquet and ranked above the chief councilors.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Jinan; on passing the capital he was invited to a banquet and seated above the chief councilors.

sentences.zh: 承安二年，移守南京，尋改知彰德府，卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Cheng'an he was transferred to defend the Southern Capital; soon he was changed to administer Zhangde Prefecture and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Cheng'an he was transferred to the Southern Capital; soon after he was made administrator of Zhangde and died.

sentences.zh: 訃聞，上遣宣徽使白琬燒飯，賻物甚厚。

translations.literal: When the death report arrived, the emperor sent the commissioner of the palace secretariat Bai Wan to offer burnt offerings; funeral gifts were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: On news of his death the emperor sent Commissioner Bai Wan to offer funeral rites, with lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 元忠素貴，性粗豪而內深忌，世宗嘗責之。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong had long been noble; by nature he was rough and bold yet inwardly deeply jealous; Shizong once reproved him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong had long been eminent; outwardly rough and bold, inwardly deeply jealous — Shizong had once rebuked him for it.

sentences.zh: 又所至不能戢奴僕，世以此為訾云。

translations.literal: Moreover wherever he went he could not restrain his slaves and servants; the age criticized him for this.
translations.idiomatic: He also failed to control his household slaves wherever he served, for which contemporaries criticized him.

sentences.zh: 子誼。

translations.literal: His son Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi

sentences.zh: 誼本名雄名。

translations.literal: Yi, original name Xiongming.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, whose original name was Xiongming.

sentences.zh: 大定八年，尚海陵女。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dading he married a daughter of Hailing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Dading he married a daughter of Hailing.

sentences.zh: 宴宗室及六品以上官，命婦預焉，上曰：「此女亦太祖之曾孫，猶朕之女，乃父廢亡，非其女之罪也。

translations.literal: At a banquet for the imperial clan and officials of the sixth rank and above, consorts were also invited; the emperor said: "This woman too is a great-granddaughter of Taizu, like a daughter to me; her father was deposed and perished — it is not her crime."
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet for the imperial clan and officials of the sixth rank and above, consorts were invited as well; the emperor said, "She too is Taizu's great-granddaughter, no different from my own daughter; her father was deposed and destroyed — that is not her fault."

sentences.zh: 」海陵女卒，大定二十一年，尚顯宗女廣平郡主。

translations.literal: " When Hailing's daughter died, in the twenty-first year of Dading he married the Princess of Guangping Commandery, a daughter of Emperor Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: " After Hailing's daughter died, in the twenty-first year of Dading he married the Princess of Guangping, a daughter of Emperor Xianzong.

sentences.zh: 誼歷仕宮衛，為人粗豪類其父。

translations.literal: Yi successively served in the palace guard; in character he was rough and bold like his father.
translations.idiomatic: Yi served in the palace guard and was rough and overbearing like his father.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，上謂原王曰：「元忠勿望其可復相也。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the emperor said to Prince Yuan: "Do not expect that Yuanzhong can again serve as chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year the emperor told Prince Yuan, "Do not expect Yuanzhong to become chief councilor again.

sentences.zh: 雄名又不及乃父，朕嘗宥待，殊不知恩，汝宜知其為人。

translations.literal: Xiongming is still less than his father; I once treated him with leniency, yet he did not know gratitude — you should understand what sort of man he is."
translations.idiomatic: Xiongming is even less capable than his father; I once showed him leniency, yet he showed no gratitude — you should know what manner of man he is."

sentences.zh: 」謂平章政事襄曰：「雄名可令補外。

translations.literal: " He said to the chief councilor Xiang: "Xiongming may be ordered to fill an outside post.
translations.idiomatic: " He told Chief Councilor Xiang, "Xiongming should be sent to a provincial post.

sentences.zh: 自今宮掖官已有旨補外者，比及廷授，即毋令入宮。

translations.literal: From now on, for palace officials who have already received orders to fill outside posts, as soon as court appointment is made they must not be allowed to enter the palace."
translations.idiomatic: From now on, whenever a palace official has been ordered to a provincial post, he must not enter the palace again once the court appointment is issued."

sentences.zh: 」於是，誼除同知澄州軍州事。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Yi was removed to associate administrator of Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " Yi was then appointed associate administrator of Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 章宗即位，廣平郡主進封鄴國長公主，誼改順天軍節度副使，加駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: When Zhangzong ascended the throne, the Princess of Guangping Commandery was advanced to Grand Princess of Ye; Yi was changed to deputy military governor of the Shuntian army and additionally made commandant of the imperial sons-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangzong ascended the throne, the Princess of Guangping was promoted to Grand Princess of Ye; Yi became deputy military governor of Shuntian and was again made commandant of the imperial sons-in-law.

sentences.zh: 承安元年，累遷秘書監兼吏部侍郎，改刑部，遷工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Cheng'an he was repeatedly promoted to director of the Secretariat and concurrent vice minister of personnel, was changed to the Ministry of Punishments, and was transferred to minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Cheng'an he rose through posts as director of the Secretariat and concurrent vice minister of personnel, then minister of punishments, and finally minister of works.

sentences.zh: 泰和元年，遇父元忠憂。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taihe he encountered mourning for his father Yuanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taihe he entered mourning for his father Yuanzhong.

sentences.zh: 二年，以本官起復。

translations.literal: In the second year he was recalled from mourning to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was recalled from mourning to his former post.

sentences.zh: 三年，知東平府事，改知真定府事。

translations.literal: In the third year he administered Dongping Prefecture and was changed to administer Zhending Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he administered Dongping, then Zhending.

sentences.zh: 六年，伐宋，遷元帥左都監。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, when Song was invaded, he was transferred to left overseer of the commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, during the campaign against Song, he was made left overseer of the commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 七年，轉左監軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to left army overseer.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he became left army overseer.

sentences.zh: 八年，拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 大安中，知大名府。

translations.literal: During Da'an he administered Daming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Da'an reign he administered Daming.

sentences.zh: 至甯初，以謀逆伏誅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhining he was executed for plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhining reign he was executed for treason.

sentences.zh: 唐括貢

translations.literal: Tangkuo Gong
translations.idiomatic: Tangkuo Gong

sentences.zh: 唐括貢，本名達哥，太傅阿裏之子也。

translations.literal: Tangkuo Gong, original name Dage, was the son of Grand Tutor Ali.
translations.idiomatic: Tangkuo Gong, whose original name was Dage, was the son of Grand Tutor Ali.

sentences.zh: 尚世宗第四女吳國公主，授駙馬都尉，充奉御。

translations.literal: He married Princess Wu of State, the fourth daughter of Emperor Shizong, was appointed commandant of the imperial sons-in-law, and served as imperial attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He married Princess Wu, the fourth daughter of Emperor Shizong, was made commandant of the imperial sons-in-law, and served as imperial attendant.

sentences.zh: 特授拱衛直副都指揮使，五遷刑部侍郎，坐擅離職削官一階，出為德州防禦使。

translations.literal: He was specially appointed deputy commander of the Archery Guard Direct Office, was promoted five times to vice minister of punishments, was demoted one rank for leaving his post without authorization, and went out as defender-in-chief of De Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially made deputy commander of the Archery Guard, rose five times to vice minister of punishments, was demoted one rank for unauthorized absence, and sent out as defender-in-chief of Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 升順天軍節度使，移鎮橫海。

translations.literal: He was promoted to military governor of the Shuntian army and transferred to command Henghai.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to military governor of Shuntian and transferred to Henghai.

sentences.zh: 召為左宣徽使，遷兵部尚書，改吏部，轉禮部尚書、兼大理卿。

translations.literal: He was recalled as left commissioner of the palace secretariat, was transferred to minister of war, was changed to minister of personnel, and was transferred to minister of rites and concurrent chief judge of Dali.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as left commissioner of the palace secretariat, served as minister of war and then personnel, and finally as minister of rites and concurrent chief judge of Dali.

sentences.zh: 先是，大理卿闕，世宗命宰臣選可授者，左丞張汝弼舉西京副留守楊子益法律詳明。

translations.literal: Earlier the post of chief judge of Dali was vacant; Shizong ordered the chief ministers to select someone suitable; the left vice minister Zhang Rubi recommended the Western Capital's deputy defender Yang Ziyi as detailed and clear in law.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the chief judgeship of Dali fell vacant, Shizong ordered the chief ministers to nominate a candidate; Left Vice Minister Zhang Rubi recommended Yang Ziyi, deputy defender of the Western Capital, as expert in law.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「子益雖明法，而用心不正，豈可任之以分別天下是非也？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Ziyi may be clear in law, but his heart is not upright — how can he be entrusted to distinguish right and wrong throughout the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Ziyi may know the law, but his heart is not upright — how can he be entrusted to judge right and wrong for the empire?"

sentences.zh: 大理須用公正人。

translations.literal: Dali must employ a fair man.
translations.idiomatic: Dali requires a man of integrity.

sentences.zh: 」左丞粘割斡特剌舉貢可任以閑簡部分而兼領是職，遂以貢為之。

translations.literal: " The left vice minister Niancha Wotela recommended Gong as able, with leisure and simplicity in disposition, to hold this office concurrently, and Gong was therefore appointed.
translations.idiomatic: " Left Vice Minister Niancha Wotela recommended Gong as a man of leisure and sound judgment who could hold the post concurrently, and Gong was appointed.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，拜樞密副使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was appointed vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he was appointed vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 章宗立，為御史大夫。

translations.literal: When Zhangzong ascended the throne, he became censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangzong ascended the throne, he became censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 會貢生日，右丞相襄、參知政事劉瑋、吏部郎中肼、中都兵馬都指揮使和喜為貢壽，遂犯夜禁，和喜遣軍人送襄至第。

translations.literal: It happened to be Gong's birthday; the right chief minister Xiang, the participant in governance Liu Wei, the director of the personnel bureau Bing, and the overall commander of troops at the Central Capital Hexi came to congratulate Gong on his birthday and thereby violated the night curfew; Hexi sent soldiers to escort Xiang to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: On Gong's birthday the right chief minister Xiang, Participant in Governance Liu Wei, Director Bing of the personnel bureau, and Central Capital commander Hexi came to celebrate and violated the night curfew; Hexi sent soldiers to escort Xiang home.

sentences.zh: 監察御史徒單德勝劾其事，下刑部逮肼等問狀。

translations.literal: Supervising censor Tudan Desheng impeached the matter; the Ministry of Punishments was ordered to arrest Bing and the others and examine the case.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Censor Tudan Desheng impeached them; the Ministry of Punishments arrested Bing and the others for questioning.

sentences.zh: 上以襄、瑋大臣釋之，而貢等各解職。

translations.literal: The emperor released Xiang and Wei as great ministers, while Gong and the others each resigned their offices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor released the great ministers Xiang and Wei, while Gong and the others resigned their posts.

sentences.zh: 尋知大興府事，復為樞密副使。

translations.literal: Soon he administered Daxing Prefecture and again became vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He soon administered Daxing and was again appointed vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 乞致仕不許，進樞密使，封莘國公，改封蕭。

translations.literal: He requested retirement but was not permitted; he was advanced to commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, enfeoffed as Duke of Xin, and his enfeoffment was changed to Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: His request to retire was denied; he was promoted to commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, enfeoffed as Duke of Xin, and later as Duke of Xiao.

sentences.zh: 復上表乞退，上曰：「向已嘗告，續知意欲外除，今之告將復若何。

translations.literal: He again submitted a memorial requesting withdrawal; the emperor said: "You already petitioned before, and I then learned you wished for an outside appointment — what is this present petition again?"
translations.idiomatic: He submitted another memorial asking to retire; the emperor said, "You already asked once, and I understood you wanted a provincial post — what do you mean by asking again?"

sentences.zh: 」遂優詔許之。

translations.literal: " An indulgent edict thereupon permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: " A gracious edict then granted his request.

sentences.zh: 尋起知真定府事。

translations.literal: Soon he was raised up to administer Zhending Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to administer Zhending.

sentences.zh: 泰和二年，薨。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taihe he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Taihe.

sentences.zh: 烏林答琳

translations.literal: Wulinda Lin
translations.idiomatic: Wulinda Lin

sentences.zh: 烏林答琳，本名留住。

translations.literal: Wulinda Lin, original name Liuzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Wulinda Lin, whose original name was Liuzhu.

sentences.zh: 尚郜國公主，加駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: He married Princess Gao of State and was additionally made commandant of the imperial sons-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: He married Princess Gao and was made commandant of the imperial sons-in-law.

sentences.zh: 貞祐元年為靜難軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenyou he was military governor of the Jingnan army.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenyou he was military governor of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 夏人犯邠州，琳降。

translations.literal: When the Xia people attacked Bin Prefecture, Lin surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tanguts attacked Binzhou, Lin surrendered.

sentences.zh: 會延安府遣通事張福孫至夏國，夏人使福孫見琳，時已中風，公主令人以狀付福孫，屬以懇禱朝廷，冀早太平得還鄉之意。

translations.literal: It happened that Yan'an Prefecture sent interpreter Zhang Fusun to the Xia state; the Xia had Fusun see Lin, who by then had suffered a stroke; the princess had someone give Fusun a written statement, entrusting him to plead earnestly with the court, hoping for early peace and return home.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan'an sent interpreter Zhang Fusun to Xia, the Tanguts had him visit Lin, who had already suffered a stroke; the princess gave Fusun a written plea begging the court to restore peace so they might return home.

sentences.zh: 福孫具以聞，詔賜以藥物。

translations.literal: Fusun reported all of this in full; an edict ordered medicines to be bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Fusun reported everything; the court ordered medicines sent to them.

sentences.zh: 徒單公弼

translations.literal: Tudan Gongbi
translations.idiomatic: Tudan Gongbi

sentences.zh: 徒單公弼，本名習烈，河北東路算主海猛安人。

translations.literal: Tudan Gongbi, original name Xilie, was a man of the Suanzhuhai meng'an on the Hebei East Route.
translations.idiomatic: Tudan Gongbi, whose original name was Xilie, was from the Suanzhuhai meng'an on the Hebei East Route.

sentences.zh: 父府君奴，尚熙宗女，加駙馬都尉，終武定軍節度使。

translations.literal: His father Fujunnu married a daughter of Emperor Xizong, was additionally made commandant of the imperial sons-in-law, and ended as military governor of the Wuding army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fujunnu married a daughter of Emperor Xizong, was made commandant of the imperial sons-in-law, and ended his career as military governor of Wuding.

sentences.zh: 公弼初充奉御，大定二十七年，尚世宗女息國公主，加定遠大將軍、駙馬都尉，改器物局直長。

translations.literal: Gongbi first served as imperial attendant; in the twenty-seventh year of Dading he married Princess Xi of State, a daughter of Emperor Shizong, was given the additional title of General Who Establishes the Distance and commandant of the imperial sons-in-law, and was changed to director of the Bureau of Implements.
translations.idiomatic: Gongbi began as an imperial attendant; in the twenty-seventh year of Dading he married Princess Xi, a daughter of Emperor Shizong, was made general who establishes the distance and commandant of the imperial sons-in-law, and appointed director of the Bureau of Implements.

sentences.zh: 轉副使、兼近侍局直長。

translations.literal: He was transferred to deputy director and concurrently director of the Bureau of Close Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He became deputy director and concurrent director of the Bureau of Close Attendance.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，起復本局副使。

translations.literal: On his father's mourning he was recalled from mourning to his former post as deputy director of the bureau.
translations.idiomatic: After entering mourning for his father he was recalled to his former post as deputy director.

sentences.zh: 章宗秋山射中虎，虎怒突而前，侍衛皆避去，公弼不動，虎亦隨斃。

translations.literal: When Zhangzong on the autumn hunt shot a tiger, the tiger in rage charged forward; the guards all fled, but Gongbi did not move, and the tiger thereupon also died.
translations.idiomatic: On an autumn hunt Zhangzong shot a tiger that charged in fury; the guards all fled, but Gongbi stood his ground until the tiger fell dead.

sentences.zh: 詔責侍衛而慰諭公弼。

translations.literal: An edict reproved the guards and comforted Gongbi with praise.
translations.idiomatic: An edict rebuked the guards and praised Gongbi for his steadiness.

sentences.zh: 除濱州刺史，再遷兵部侍郎，累除知大名府事。

translations.literal: He was removed to prefect of Bin Prefecture, was twice transferred to vice minister of war, and repeatedly served as administrator of Daming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Bin, twice promoted to vice minister of war, and repeatedly served as administrator of Daming.

sentences.zh: 是時，伐宋軍興，有司督逋租及牛頭稅甚急，公弼奏：「軍士從戎，民亦疲弊，可緩徵以紓民。

translations.literal: At that time the campaign against Song had begun; the authorities pressed collection of overdue rents and the ox-head tax very urgently; Gongbi memorialized: "Soldiers follow the army, and the people too are exhausted — collection may be slowed to relieve the people."
translations.idiomatic: During the war against Song the authorities pressed hard for overdue rents and the ox-head tax; Gongbi memorialized, "The soldiers are at war and the people are exhausted — collections should be eased to relieve them."

sentences.zh: 」朝廷從之。

translations.literal: " The court accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: " The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 大安初，知大興府事，讞武清盜，疑其有冤，已而果獲真盜。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Da'an he administered Daxing Prefecture; in judging a theft case at Wuqing he suspected there was a miscarriage of justice, and afterward the true thief was indeed captured.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Da'an reign he administered Daxing; in a theft case at Wuqing he suspected a wrongful conviction, and the real thief was later caught.

sentences.zh: 歲餘拜參知政事，進右丞，轉左丞。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was appointed participant in governance, advanced to right vice minister, and transferred to left vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he was made participant in governance, then right vice minister, then left vice minister.

sentences.zh: 至甯初，拜平章政事，封定國公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhining he was appointed chief councilor and enfeoffed as Duke of Ding.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhining he was made chief councilor and enfeoffed as Duke of Ding.

sentences.zh: 貞祐初，進拜右丞相，罷知中山府事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyou he was advanced to right chief minister and dismissed from administering Zhongshan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenyou he was promoted to right chief minister and relieved of his post at Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 是時，中都圍急不可行，圍解，宣宗曰：「中山新被兵，不如河中善。

translations.literal: At that time the Central Capital was under tight siege and travel was impossible; when the siege was lifted, Xuanzong said: "Zhongshan has newly suffered warfare — Hezhong is better."
translations.idiomatic: The Central Capital was then under siege and the journey impossible; when the siege lifted, Xuanzong said, "Zhongshan has just seen fighting — Hezhong would be safer."

sentences.zh: 」乃改知河中府。

translations.literal: " He was therefore changed to administer Hezhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " He was reassigned to administer Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 曆定國軍節度使事、太孫太師、同判大睦親府事。

translations.literal: He successively served as military governor of the Dingguo army, grand preceptor to the heir apparent, and associate judge of the Great Office of Imperial Kin.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as military governor of Dingguo, grand preceptor to the heir apparent, and associate judge of the Great Office of Imperial Kin.

sentences.zh: 興定五年薨，宣宗輟朝，賻贈，諡恪願。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xingding he died; Xuanzong suspended court, granted funeral gifts, and gave the posthumous name Keyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of Xingding; Xuanzong suspended court, granted lavish funeral gifts, and gave him the posthumous name Keyuan.

sentences.zh: 徒單銘

translations.literal: Tudan Ming
translations.idiomatic: Tudan Ming

sentences.zh: 贊曰：天子娶后，王姬下嫁，豈不重哉。

translations.literal: The commentator says: The Son of Heaven takes a queen; royal daughters marry down — is this not weighty?
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: When the Son of Heaven takes a queen and royal daughters marry downward, the matter is weighty indeed.

sentences.zh: 秦、漢以來，無世世甥舅之家。

translations.literal: From Qin and Han onward there have been no families of maternal uncles and nephews generation after generation.
translations.idiomatic: Since Qin and Han there had been no clans that remained consort kin generation after generation.

sentences.zh: 《關雎》之道缺，外戚驕盈，《何彼穠矣》不作，王姬肅雝之義幾希矣。

translations.literal: The way of the "Ospreys" was lacking; consort kin grew arrogant and full; the "How Luxuriant" was not composed; the righteous dignity of royal daughters marrying down was nearly lost.
translations.idiomatic: The ideal of the "Ospreys" was lost, consort kin grew arrogant, the "How Luxuriant" went unheeded, and the solemn propriety of royal daughters marrying downward nearly vanished.

sentences.zh: 蓋古者異姓世爵公侯與天子為昏因，他姓不得參焉。

translations.literal: For in antiquity only enfeoffed lords of different surnames with hereditary noble rank formed marriage alliances with the Son of Heaven; other surnames could not participate.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity only hereditary noble houses of distinct surnames married into the imperial line; no others could share that privilege.

sentences.zh: 女為王后，己尚王姬，而自貴其貴，富厚不加焉，寵榮不與焉。

translations.literal: When one's daughter became queen, one had already married a royal daughter, and thus honored one's own honor — wealth and rank were not increased, favor and glory were not granted.
translations.idiomatic: When a daughter became empress, the house had already married a princess; it rested on its existing dignity — no added wealth, rank, or favor.

sentences.zh: 使漢、唐行此道，則無呂氏、王氏、武氏之難，公主下嫁各安其分、各得其所矣。

translations.literal: Had Han and Tang followed this way, there would have been no disasters of the Lü, Wang, and Wu clans; princesses marrying down would each have kept their place and found their proper station.
translations.idiomatic: Had Han and Tang followed this practice, there would have been no catastrophes of the Lü, Wang, and Wu clans, and princesses would each have kept their proper place.

sentences.zh: 金之徒單、拿懶、唐括、蒲察、裴滿、紇石烈、僕散皆貴族也，天子娶後必於是，公主下嫁必於是，與周之齊、紀無異，此昏禮之最得宜者，盛于漢、唐矣。

translations.literal: Jin's Tudan, Nalan, Tangkuo, Pucha, Peiman, Hesheli, and Pusan were all noble clans; the Son of Heaven taking a queen had to be from them, and princesses marrying down had to be to them — no different from Zhou's Qi and Ji — this marriage ritual was most fitting, surpassing Han and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: The Tudan, Nalan, Tangkuo, Pucha, Peiman, Hesheli, and Pusan clans of Jin were all noble houses; emperors took empresses only from them and princesses married only into them — as in Zhou's Qi and Ji — the most proper marriage system, surpassing even Han and Tang.

sentences.zh: 徒單四喜

translations.literal: Tudan Sixi
translations.idiomatic: Tudan Sixi

sentences.zh: 徒單四喜，哀宗皇后之弟也。

translations.literal: Tudan Sixi was the younger brother of Aizong's empress.
translations.idiomatic: Tudan Sixi was the younger brother of Empress Tudan, consort of Emperor Aizong.

sentences.zh: 天興二年正月辛酉夜，四喜、內侍馬福惠至自歸德，時河朔已失利，京城猶未知，二人被旨迎兩宮，遂託以報捷，執小黃旗以入，至則奏兩宮以奉迎之意。

translations.literal: On the night of xinyou, the first month of the second year of Tianxing, Sixi and the inner attendant Ma Fuhui arrived from Guide; at that time the north of the Yellow River had already been lost, but the capital still did not know; the two men received orders to welcome the two palaces; they therefore pretended to report victory, entered holding small yellow banners, and upon arrival reported to the two palaces the intention to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinyou night of the first month in the second year of Tianxing, Sixi and the inner attendant Ma Fuhui arrived from Guide; the Hebei region had already fallen, though the capital did not yet know; ordered to welcome the two palaces, they pretended to bring news of victory, entered with small yellow banners, and reported the plan to welcome the empresses.

sentences.zh: 是日，召二相入議，二相及烏古孫奴申諫不可行。

translations.literal: That day the two chief ministers were summoned to deliberate; the two chief ministers and Wugusun Nushen remonstrated that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: That day the two chief ministers were summoned; they and Wugusun Nushen urged that the plan must not proceed.

sentences.zh: 四喜作色曰：「我奉制旨迎兩宮，有敢言不行者，當以別敕從事矣。

translations.literal: Sixi changed color and said: "I carry an imperial order to welcome the two palaces — whoever dares say it cannot be done will be dealt with by separate edict."
translations.idiomatic: Sixi flushed and said, "I carry an imperial order to welcome the two palaces — anyone who dares oppose it will be punished by special edict."

sentences.zh: 」二相不復敢言，行議遂決。

translations.literal: " The two chief ministers dared speak no more, and the plan to proceed was decided.
translations.idiomatic: " The two chief ministers fell silent, and the departure was decided.

sentences.zh: 制旨所取兩宮、柔妃裴滿氏及令人張秀蕊、都轄、承御、湯藥、皇乳母鞏國夫人等十餘人外，皆放遣之。
