translations.literal: Apart from the two palaces, the Gentle Consort of the Peiman clan, the Lady-in-Waiting Zhang Xiurui, the director of attendance, the imperial attendants, the medicine staff, the imperial wet nurse the Lady of Gong, and more than ten others specified by the order, all were dismissed and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order only the two palaces, Gentle Consort Peiman, Lady-in-Waiting Zhang Xiurui, the director of attendance, imperial attendants, medicine staff, the imperial wet nurse Lady of Gong, and a dozen others were taken; the rest were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 又取宮中寶物，馬蹄金四百杖、大珠如栗黃者七千杖、生金山一、龍腦板二及信瑞御璽，仍許賜忠孝軍以兩宮隨行物之半。

translations.literal: They also took palace treasures: four hundred bars of hoof-shaped gold, seven thousand large pearls yellow as chestnuts, one raw-gold mountain, two boards of borneol, and the imperial seals of trust and auspice; it was also permitted to grant the Loyal and Filial Army half of the two palaces' traveling goods.
translations.idiomatic: They also seized palace treasures: four hundred bars of hoof-shaped gold, seven thousand large yellow pearls, one raw-gold mountain, two boards of borneol, and the imperial seals of trust and auspice, and allowed the Loyal and Filial Army half of the two palaces' traveling goods.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，太后御仁安殿，出錠金及七寶金洗分賜忠孝軍。

translations.literal: On renyin the empress dowager presided at Rén'an Hall, brought out ingot gold and seven-jeweled gold basins, and distributed them to the Loyal and Filial Army.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin the empress dowager sat in Ren'an Hall and distributed ingot gold and seven-jeweled basins to the Loyal and Filial Army.

sentences.zh: 是夜，兩宮騎而出，至陳留，見城外二三處火起，疑有兵，遲回間，奴申初不欲行，即承太后旨馳還。

translations.literal: That night the two palaces rode out; reaching Chenliu they saw two or three fires outside the walls and suspected troops; while hesitating, Nushen, who from the first had not wished to go, received the empress dowager's order and galloped back.
translations.idiomatic: That night the two palaces rode out; at Chenliu they saw fires outside the walls and suspected an ambush; while they hesitated, Nushen, who had opposed the journey from the start, received the empress dowager's order and galloped back.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，入京頓四喜家，少頃，還宮。

translations.literal: On guimao they entered the capital and lodged at Sixi's house; after a short while they returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao they entered the capital and rested at Sixi's house, then soon returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 復議以是夜再往，太后憊于鞍馬不能動，遂止。

translations.literal: They again deliberated going out that same night; the empress dowager was exhausted from horseback and could not move, and so it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: They debated setting out again that night, but the empress dowager was too exhausted from riding to continue, and the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 明日，崔立變。

translations.literal: The next day Cui Li mutinied.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Cui Li rebelled.

sentences.zh: 四喜、術甲塔失不及塔失不之父咬住、四喜妻完顏氏，以忠孝卒九十七騎奪曹門而出，將往歸德，不得出，轉陳州門，亦為門卒所止。

translations.literal: Sixi, Shujia Tashibuji, Tashibuji's father Yaozhu, and Sixi's wife of the Wanyan clan, with ninety-seven Loyal and Filial cavalrymen, seized the Cao Gate and went out, intending to go to Guide but unable to get out; turning to the Chenzhou Gate, they were also stopped by the gate guards.
translations.idiomatic: Sixi, Shujia Tashibuji, Tashibuji's father Yaozhu, and Sixi's Wanyan wife, with ninety-seven Loyal and Filial horsemen, forced the Cao Gate and tried to reach Guide but could not get out; at the Chenzhou Gate they were stopped as well.

sentences.zh: 門帥裕州防禦使阿不罕斜合已遁去，經歷官完顏合住權帥職，麾門卒放塔失不等去，且曰：「罪在我，非汝等之過。

translations.literal: The gate commander, defender-in-chief of Yu Prefecture Abuhan Xiehe, had already fled; the administrative officer Wanyan Hezhu acted in the commander's place, ordered the gate guards to release Tashibuji and the others, and said: "The guilt is mine, not yours."
translations.idiomatic: The gate commander, Defender-in-Chief Abuhan Xiehe of Yuzhou, had fled; Acting Commander Wanyan Hezhu ordered the guards to let Tashibuji and the others go, saying, "The blame is mine, not yours."

sentences.zh: 」明日，立以數十騎召合住，合住自分必死，易衣冠而往。

translations.literal: " The next day Li summoned Hezhu with several dozen horsemen; Hezhu judged that he would certainly die, changed his robes, and went.
translations.idiomatic: " The next day Li summoned Hezhu with several dozen horsemen; expecting death, Hezhu changed his clothes and went.

sentences.zh: 立左右扼腕欲加刃。

translations.literal: Li's attendants clutched their wrists, ready to apply blades.
translations.idiomatic: Li's men gripped their swords, ready to strike.

sentences.zh: 立遙見，問：「汝是放忠孝軍出門者耶？

translations.literal: Li saw him from afar and asked: "Are you the one who released the Loyal and Filial Army through the gate?"
translations.idiomatic: Li called from a distance, "Are you the man who let the Loyal and Filial Army out the gate?"

sentences.zh: 」合住曰：「然。

translations.literal: " Hezhu said: "Yes.
translations.idiomatic: " Hezhu said, "I am.

sentences.zh: 天子使命，某實放之，罪在某。

translations.literal: It was the Son of Heaven's command — I indeed released them; the guilt is mine."
translations.idiomatic: It was the emperor's order — I released them; the blame is mine."

sentences.zh: 」立忽若有所省，顧群卒言：「此官人我識之，前築裏城時與我同事。

translations.literal: " Li suddenly seemed to remember something and said to the troops: "I know this official — when we built the inner wall before, he worked with me.
translations.idiomatic: " Li seemed to remember and told his men, "I know this official — we worked together when the inner wall was built.

sentences.zh: 我所部十餘卒盜官木罪當死，此官人不之問，但笞數十而已。

translations.literal: More than ten soldiers under my command stole official timber — the crime deserved death — but this official did not pursue it and only had them beaten several dozen strokes.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten of my men stole official timber, a capital crime, but he only had them beaten a few dozen strokes.

sentences.zh: 此家能殺人，能救人。

translations.literal: This house can kill men and can save men."
translations.idiomatic: This man can kill and he can save."

sentences.zh: 」因好謂合住曰：「業已放出，吾不汝罪也。」

translations.literal: " He then spoke kindly to Hezhu: "They are already released — I will not punish you."
translations.idiomatic: " He then said kindly to Hezhu, "They are already gone — I will not punish you."

sentences.zh: 四喜等至歸德，上驚問「兩宮何如？

translations.literal: When Sixi and the others reached Guide, the emperor asked in alarm: "How are the two palaces?"
translations.idiomatic: When Sixi and the others reached Guide, the emperor asked in alarm, "How are the two palaces?"

sentences.zh: 」二人奏「京城軍變，不及入宮。

translations.literal: " The two men reported: "There was a military mutiny in the capital — we could not enter the palace."
translations.idiomatic: " They reported, "The capital mutinied — we could not reach the palace."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「汝父汝妻獨得出耶？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Only your father and your wife got out?"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Only your father and your wife escaped?"

sentences.zh: 」下之獄，皆斬於市。

translations.literal: " They were cast into prison and all beheaded in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: " They were imprisoned and beheaded in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：四喜奉迎兩宮，而值崔立之變，智者居此，與兩宮周旋兵間，以俟事變之定而徐圖之。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Sixi was to welcome the two palaces but encountered Cui Li's mutiny; a wise man in this position would move with the two palaces amid the soldiers, waiting for affairs to settle and then planning slowly.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Sixi was sent to welcome the two palaces but met Cui Li's mutiny; a wise man would have stayed with them amid the troops, waited for events to settle, and only then planned their escape.

sentences.zh: 萬一不然，以一死徇之耳，他無策也。

translations.literal: If that were not possible, to die for them with one death — there is no other stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: If that failed, he should have died with them — there was no other honorable course.

sentences.zh: 四喜奉其私親以歸，而望人主貸其死，豈非愚乎！

translations.literal: Sixi brought his private kin home and yet hoped the sovereign would spare his life — is this not foolish!
translations.idiomatic: Sixi saved his own kin and still hoped the emperor would spare him — was that not folly!
